Find the area between the curve $y=-2{x}^{2}-9$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-2{x}^{2}-9)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-9{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-9\cdot x{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-2(\frac{(2)^{3}}{3}-0)-9(2-0) \\  & =-\frac{16}{3}-18 \\  & =-\frac{70}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\frac{70}{3}.$
